articleTitle: Performance comparison of applying integer and fractional order calculus to DC motor speed control experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Fractional order calculus has been widely studied because it is suspected to perform better than integer one, particularly in control system applications. The performance comparison of the two methods on the derivative and integral orders is fascinating. Experimental application studies will strengthen validation compared to just going through simulations. This research aims to compare the performance of integer and fractional orders on the implementation of DC motor speed control. The experimental results indicated that the fractional order calculus method was commonly more satisfactory than the integer one both in accuracy and convergent rate in controlling DC motor speed. Additionally, it enhanced its accuracy by approximately 2% for integral gain and up to 12% for differential one. However, the integer order calculus approach has a faster settling time and better stability than the fractional order technique in the case of differential gain

articleTitle: A Novel Radar Receiver for Joint Radar And Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Integration of radar and communication systems on the same platform reveals the interference problems of these systems, as well as the installation problems on small scale platforms. Joint radar and communication systems have significant potential in solving these problems, as they reduce congestion both in the spectrum and on the platform. In this article, the integration of communication symbols into the radar signal is studied and a new technique for mono-static pulsed radar receiver is proposed to obtain a better range and velocity estimation performance. The effects of the integration methods on the performance of the radar receiver are analysed.

articleTitle: Observation of Glucose Concentration in Water using Surface Plasmon Resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based biosensor in the Kretschmann configuration is used to detect glucose concentration. Here, we use SPR sensor, both experimentally and in simulation, for refractive index sensing where glucose solution of various concentrations is chosen as model. For the experiment part, the varied glucose concentrations were injected into a small reaction chamber encapsulating the non-functionalized thin gold (Au) SPR film, where the reflectivity and resonance angle changes were monitored in real-time. Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) was conducted to simulate the plasmon resonance modulation under various concentration dependent refractive indices. As the sensing descriptors, we utilized resonance angle and half width at half maximum (HWHM). As a result, both resonance angle and HWHM increase linearly to glucose concentration.

articleTitle: Visible Light Trapping in Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell with Vanadium-Doped ZnO as Back Reflector Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The back reflector layer (BRL) has been integrated with DSSC in the present work. The BRL was developed from zinc acetate dehydrate, ammonium metavanadate, and methanol as the precursor. The V:ZnO solution was deposited on the glass substrate using the spray technique, while the DSSC was fabricated by the screen-printing technique. Several characterizations were conducted following XRD for their structure, SEM for their morphology, absorption, transmittance, and reflectance spectra to study their optical properties. Then, the BRL was integrated with DSSC on the rear side. The V-I analysis shows the improvement of all photovoltaic parameters, not only EFF but also their FF, $V_{oc}, J_{sc}, V_{\max}, J_{\max}$, and $I_{sc}$. The highest DSSC efficiency was found for V:ZnO 15s (EFF = 1.93 %), allowing the efficiency enhancement of 6.74% from the control DSSC.

articleTitle: Ripeness Classification of Cavendish Bananas using Multi-object Detection Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Cavendish bananas, recognized for their global economic and nutritional value, often pose challenges in ensuring consistent ripeness quality throughout the supply chain, which is essential for efficient post-harvest management and ensuring optimal consumer experience. Traditional methods, reliant on human visual inspection, are subjective and inconsistent. This paper proposes a novel multi-object detection approach for accurately classifying the ripeness of multiple Cavendish bananas in an image using computer vision and deep learning techniques. We employed the Yolov5 model, a state-of-the-art object detection architecture using a standardized ripeness classification system to simultaneously identify and categorize every banana in an image. To train the model, a diverse dataset of 600 Cavendish banana bunches at different ripeness stages was collected, augmented, and annotated with ground truth labels. Training result shows that the multi-object detection network successfully delineates the bananas in input images while simultaneously predicting their ripeness classes. The proposed approach achieves 98.8% mean average precision, 90.5% precision, and 92.6% recall, even when the test images contain overlapping bananas and diverse background colors. The compact size of the object detection model, made it applicable to an embedded system, enabling realtime ripeness classification of Cavendish bananas with simple image uploads from handheld devices. This research contributes to the advancement of agricultural technology and opens avenues for future studies in fruit ripeness analysis and food quality assessment.

articleTitle: Palm Fruit Ripeness Characteristics Specification Using Free Space Measurement Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Oil palm fruits has thick flesh and is rich in oil, and the oil content increases according to the maturity of the fruit. Many methods are developed to detect the maturity level of oil palm fruits, such as destructive and non-destructive methods. The destructive techniques involve physical contact that disrupts the palm fruits’s integrity and significantly diminishes the oil yield obtainable from the palm fruits being analyzed. Meanwhile, non-destructive techniques can involve non-contact features that are either visual or non-visual. This research aims to utilize the Free Space Measurement (FSM) approach as a non-destructive method to determine the characteristics of the maturity level of oil palm fruits. The study will analyze three different levels of maturity: unripe, ripe, and overripe. The results obtained state that unripe fruit has a smaller transmission coefficient compared to ripe fruit. This is due to raw fruit having a low water content. Therefore, the level of transmission of electromagnetic waves is also low. Ripe fruit has a higher transmission coefficient than overripe fruit due to the presence of free fatty acids in the overripe fruit, which negatively impacts the oil’s quality.

articleTitle: Fast Response Nonlinear Injection Control of Isolated DC-DC Converter for Cable-based Seabed Observatory Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The paper presents the design of a controller for a current-fed isolated step-down DC-DC converter, which serves as the power supply for cable-based seabed sensors. The controller includes nonlinear compensation of unknown load, as previously proposed, and additional proportional-integral feedback that enhances the fast response as 10 times the natural response while maintaining the system’s stability, even with several converters put in a series. The system’s output voltage is controllable, even when the output current is null. The analyses of zero and poles are shown, and the method to calculate the gain coefficients of the controller is also presented. The new coefficient $\zeta$ is easily conceivable and is introduced as a calculation parameter. Simulation using Matlab - Simulink - Simscape confirms the results obtained.

articleTitle: New Improved Sierpinski Carpet Structures Based Thinned Planar Array to Synthesize Low Sidelobes Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for generating new fractal structures characterized by its ability to reduce the number of elements in planar arrays while providing the desired beam figuration demand. The main challenges for creating fractal arrays such as the Sierpinski carpet are the high sidelobe level (SLL) as well as the large number of radiating elements in the higher growth stages. In this paper, based on the traditional Sierpinski carpet, several innovative fractal array structures are proposed which are embedded with traditional fully optimized planar arrays to reduce the computational and RF chain complexities in different growth stages and make them suitable for the application of global optimization techniques. Thus, it is possible to use the genetic algorithm (GA) to improve the excitation of elements in the proposed structures to generate the desired patterns. The method depends on generating different primitive array matrices with multiple possibilities consisting of working (ON) and non-working (OFF) elements, which is the basis for building improved planar arrays. To reduce RF complexity further, amplitude-only excitation is included in the optimization process. Computational results show that the new and improved versions of the Sierpinski carpet produce lower SLL radiation patterns with fewer radiating elements than their original counterpart in the fully optimized planar arrays.

articleTitle: Water Insoluble Polyoxometalate Derivative (PW11Cs) with High Light-Reflective Properties for Counter Electrode in Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Counter electrode (CE) is a part of Dyesensitized solar cells (DSSCs) that plays roles in electron transfer due to conductive properties, redox reaction of electrolyte due to catalytic activity, and light-harvesting optimization due to light-reflecting capability. Polyoxometalates (POMs) are materials that have catalytic activity, so they are widely applied in many applications, including DSSCs. However, studies about the light-reflective properties of POMs are still limited. In this paper, we study the conductive and light-reflective characteristics of a POM material. It is water insoluble PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs which is derived from water soluble $Na_{3}PW_{12}O_{40}$. Conductivity measurements of PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs and PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs/cellulose composite films show that they have good conductivity with sheet resistance $(R_{5})$ values 6.19 $\operatorname{Ohm}(sq.)^{-1}$ and $7.11Ohm(sq.)^{-1}$, respectively. Light-reflectance spectra shows that Pt/PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs and Pt/PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs/cellulose composite films have higher light-reflective characteristics than Pt film. Based on conductivity data and light-reflectance spectra, it can be concluded that the characteristics of PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs (in both variations) fulfil the requirements as a doping material for CE in DSSCs. As consequences, with those characteristics PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs has big prospects to be utilized as dopant of Pt-based CE to enhance the performance of DSSCs.

articleTitle: Lead (Pb) Detection Analysis Based on Multimode Plastic Optical Fiber Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Heavy metal pollution in drinking water still occurs in several countries. Excessive content of heavy metals, especially lead, in drinking water can seriously impact public health, such as organ damage and even death. On the other hand, testing for lead in drinking water is still conducted on a laboratory basis, which is expensive, lengthy, and ineffective. Therefore, lead detection in water has been improved using multimode plastic optical fiber that is accessible, light, and highly sensitive. The study aims to analyze fiber optic sensor characteristics in detecting the concentration of lead (Pb) in water. The red beam behavior generated the analysis while propagated in optical fiber. The optical fiber cladding had been peeled off and soaked in the lead solution, and the photodiode was detected. It results that the output voltage is in inverse proportion to lead concentration. The sensitivity of optical fiber detection was characterized using straight and bending optical fiber. The study concluded that the bending optical fiber has wider and higher sensitivity, which is 1.34 V and 0.924 V/ppm, respectively. The results indicated that the optical fiber is compatible with lead detection applications to minimize the impact of heavy metal pollution in water.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Link Failover Using Routing Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Multi- Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The reliability of internet service provider (ISP) networks is essential to ensure uninterrupted service. However, maintaining link availability or server network device redundancy can be challenging for ISP companies with high data communication networks. In this research, we analyze the performance of the Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) network using Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) to back up the network at a commercial ISP. We use four routers for designing this system, including two PE routers as routes from two different ISPs and a router at the head office as a server gateway. Each router has a separate Autonomous System Number, and they communicate with each other using BGP routing. The novelty of our research is that we have implemented the backup system directly into the real-time network, and the downtime duration becomes smoother while maintaining 100% quality. From the simulation results of the failover system, we observe that the backup process runs smoothly and maintains network quality, which is evident from the measurement of throughput parameters of 1658 bps, delay of 244.6 ms, jitter of 0.23 ms, and 0% packet loss. Compared to using a single link connection, a failover system using BGP routing provides better results.

articleTitle: Design of K-Band Metasurface Beam Splitter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We present the design and analysis of a Huygens’ metasurfaces for beam-splitting applications in the K-band. The metasurface consists of three dielectric substrates with four etched metallic layers and is designed to operate at the center frequency of 25 GHz. By independently manipulating electric and magnetic resonances through variation in the etched metallic geometries, the device efficiently splits the incident beams in two different refraction angles. Here, we provide a preliminary analysis and numerical simulations of the device, emphasizing its relevance in creating smart wireless environments in the millimeter-wave ranges.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-proportional Controller of EPS for Autonomous Driving of Small Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Besides providing assisting torque to the driver, electric power steering (EPS) can also be used as a component of the steering system for autonomous vehicles. Using steer-by-wire (SbW) systems, the EPS dynamic mostly has a second-order one degree of freedom (DOF). This paper proposes a fuzzy-proportional controller of EPS for the autonomous driving of a small electric vehicle (EV) with the EPS dynamic having a fourth-order two DOF. First, a dual-mode EPS dynamic model is adopted, and its parameters’ values are identified through frequency response experiments. Then, a fuzzy-proportional controller is designed, and its performance is compared with that of the conventional PID controller. From the simulation results of step and chirp signal responses, the EPS system with the fuzzy-proportional controller has better tracking ability than the conventional PID controller. The system with the fuzzy-proportional controller has a smaller overshoot of 1.1% and a faster rise time of 0.139 s than the PID controller, as seen in the step response.

articleTitle: Simulation of Circular Patch Unit Cell as a Reflector on F4BMX220 Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Blank spots are an important problem that must be overcome in wireless communication. Metamaterials, with their ability to reflect electromagnetic signals with good efficiency, are believed to be able to overcome this problem. In this paper, a metamaterial with a circular patch unit-cell for reflector applications that operates at a frequency of 3.5 GHz is proposed. Software for electromagnetic analysis (CST) is used to optimize the unit cell and see its performance as a reflector. The research results obtained a 91.4% reflected power percentage, 0.005% absorbed power percentage, and a reflection angle of −6.77°. These results show that the proposed device has good properties for future reflecting intelligent applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of GoogLeNet and AlexNet Models Performances for Spine Curvature Images Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study aims to classify spinal images into two classes, namely normal and abnormal categories. The images data was taken from hospitals at Universiti Sains Malaysia. The method used in this study is deep learning method using the GoogLeNet and AlexNet models. The research process involves preprocessing, classifying spinal images using deep learning techniques and analyzing the results. The performance of both models is evaluated based on the accuracy and time in classifying the training data. The results showed that the two models, GoogLeNet and AlexNet, had good performance in classifying spine images. Both models achieve an average accuracy of 98.75 % on the training data used. These results show the potential for using deep learning methods to assist in the process of diagnosing spinal disorders using imagery. This research has important implications in the field of medicine, especially in the field of diagnosis and monitoring of spinal disorders. Deep learning methods, especially the GoogLeNet and AlexNet models, can be used as an effective and reliable tool in classifying spinal images. With this capability, it is expected to increase efficiency and accuracy in the process of diagnosis.

articleTitle: General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) Evaluation on Cyclone-V SoC FPGA Using OpenCL
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Trends in AI implementations, such as machine learning and deep learning, have been widely used in various studies. At the heart of AI computations such as speech recognition, image recognition, and processing computer graphics is general matrix multiplication, abbreviated as GEMM. AI implementation is currently attracting programmers to implement it on an FPGA. On the other hand, the latest FPGA is integrated with a Hard Processor System (HPS) to increase the productivity of system development. Here, we performed the matrix multiplication using a Cyclone V SoC FPGA integrated with ARM processors. To reduce programming complexity and speed up the process, the kernel for the FPGA was built using the OpenCL programming language. In the experiment, we conducted the matrix multiplication by employing global and local memory. We also proposed a method for estimating the peak performance based on the compilation report. According to the experimental results, the actual performance was approximately identical to the estimation. The peak performance for matrix multiplication using local memory access was 17.86 GFlops and utilized 14.2 watts of power.

articleTitle: Analytical Study on the Effect of Perovskite Layer Thickness on Photo-capacitor Device for Retinomorphic Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A retinomorphic sensor is a kind of image sensor inspired by the biological structure and function of the human retina. The sensor is promising to be used in autonomous vehicle applications and neuromorphic computation due to its rapid responses to brightness changes and low power consumption. A photo-capacitor device is utilized in retinomorphic sensors to characterize the response to light intensity changes. It works to detect light and adjust the capacitance value depending on the intensity of the light it receives. The simulation in this study uses a photo-capacitor with a bi-layer dielectric structure, with a perovskite layer acting as the light-responsive layer and a silicon dioxide layer acting as the light-unresponsive layer. The impact of perovskite layer thickness has been analyzed to discover how the electric field responds at various wavelengths. The findings demonstrate that a perovskite thickness greater than 300 nm can provide a higher electric field dispersion than one less than 300 nm. It is observed that the electric field is also proportional to the absorbance of devices. For various wavelengths, the peak of the electric field is distributed randomly.

articleTitle: Design of C-Band Microstrip Fractal Antenna Combined with Pyramidal Horn
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The current delivery method in multilevel array distribution is used to create a fractal microstrip antenna in the shape of a stacked box. The fractal antenna was chosen because it has a large antenna working bandwidth due to the repeating of the physical form of the fractal itself, giving it the appearance of a combination of many antennas that may be merged into a single fractal antenna. The proposed fractal microstrip antenna has a working bandwidth of 2.62 GHz to 5.67 GHz and a working range of 3.05 GHz. This fractal microstrip antenna is combined with a high directivity pyramidal horn to boost the antenna gain. The proposed feed antenna combines a fractal microstrip antenna and a pyramidal horn. The combination of these two antennas can produce a gain of 9.18 dB. The simulation was extended by combining the proposed antenna with a 2.4-meter-diameter parabolic reflector to meet the criteria for a ground station receiving antenna on the C-band frequency. The gain produced by this combination is 30.8 dB. The simulation result for return loss, E and H plane radiation pattern, and antenna gain, show that this antenna configuration can be used for Himawari-9 data reception.

articleTitle: Design Implementation of Flood Early Warning System for Residential Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The efforts to mitigate floods are necessary. One of the tools that can contribute to flood mitigation is the Flood Early Warning System (FEWS). The main goal of this study is to design a prototype of FEWS that can be easily used anywhere, anytime, and provide accurate water level readings. The prototype system is designed using an Ultrasonic Sensor for water level detection, an alarm system, and Blynk as a web and mobile dashboard. The prototype consists of four main components: Ultrasonic Sensor HC-SR04, Arduino Nano, NodeMCU, and HC-12. It comprises two units: a transmitter unit and a receiver unit. To determine the accuracy and consistency of the Ultrasonic Sensor, the author conducted testing using calibration, non-continuous, and continuous methods. The accuracy obtained was 99.71%. Additionally, the author observed high consistency in the readings of the ultrasonic sensor, as evident from continuous sensor reading test results. Furthermore, the receiver unit successfully displayed output according to the water level threshold for each condition. Additionally, the Blynk web and mobile dashboard were able to display output as per the design. However, we suggest adding data logging features and also solar panels as a renewable power source to support the improved prototype system.

articleTitle: Antipodal Vivaldi Array Systems for Azimuth and Elevation Beamsteering Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental analysis of beamsteering systems employing Antipodal Vivaldi arrays for controlled directional reception. The systems were configured in elevation and azimuth setup, achieving an impressive bandwidth of 800 MHz (2.2 GHz to 3 GHz). In the Azimuth setup, the azimuth antipodal Vivaldi array has a gain of 16.1 dBi while the azimuth system gain of 3.34 dBi was achieved, enabling beamsteering within ± 30 degrees. The elevation configuration attained an antenna array gain of 10.4 dBi and a system gain of -3.01 dBi, demonstrating beamsteering capabilities within ± 60 degrees. The good measured performance of the antenna systems implicates their utility in enhancing signal reception and connectivity in indoor scenarios.

articleTitle: Artificial Periodic Structures for Bandwidth and Gain Enhancement of Vivaldi Antennas used in GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this research, a Vivaldi antenna was designed for ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications which can work well at two band frequencies from 2.53-3.87 GHz and 5.276.34 GHz. The antenna is made from an FR 4 substrate with a thickness of 1.65 mm, $\epsilon _{r}=4.9$ and a copper patch material with a thickness of 0.035 mm. The basic antenna design has dimensions of 69x69 mm. To improve the performance of the antenna, an artificial periodic structure (APS) made of copper with a thickness of 0.035 mm was added which aims to widen the bandwidth, increase the gain and reduce the antenna sidelobe level. The simulation results show that the addition of 1x6 single structure APS can effectively widen the antenna’s bandwidth to 400 Mhz (30%) wider than the basic Vivaldi design, increase the gain by 1.41 dB (9.7%) and reduce the sidelobe by 0.4 dB (5.5%). Meanwhile, the addition of 2x6 single structure APS can expand the bandwidth by 460 MHz (35%) from the basic antenna design. The best performance is achieved by an antenna design with a 1x6 single APS structure.

articleTitle: Implementation of Kalman Filter for Stabilizing Ultrasonic Sensor Reading on Distilled Ethanol Levels Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Digitalization measurements, such as sensors, are growing significantly. An ethanol concentration sensor is a digital device for measuring the ethanol content in a solution. Measuring ethanol in a solution might help to identify the ethanol levels, especially in halal-food beverages or some food-agricultural products. The main issue in measuring ethanol on distilled products is the unstable surface, which could be incorrect analysis. Therefore, in this research Kalman filter algorithm was designed on an ultrasonic sensor to reduce the incorrect reading analysis. The result gave a covariance matrix of the measurement noise (Q) = 0.00001 and a covariance matrix associated with the noise in states (R) = 5999.3955 and potential to apply, which gives better accuracy and stability to the reading data.

articleTitle: Developing A Portable Electrothermal Microcantilever Read-out System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study explores the application of tipless microcantilever sensors in a portable particle detection system. The system incorporates a multi-instrument test and measurement device, a single-board computer, and a Python-based GUI for circuit communication. The performance of the system is evaluated by examining the resonance shift and analyzing the Q-factor under humidity variations.The experimental results indicate that the system exhibits stable responses under both closed and open system configurations. In open configuration, the cantilever sensor was directly exposed to the humidifier in different concentration levels. In contrary, close configuration lets the vapor particles randomly attached to the cantilever beam in a chamber. Here, the humidity of the chamber was measured using a relative humidity meter. The phase difference during resonance frequency shows a standard deviation of 1.912° for the closed system and 4.30° for the open system. The study confirms that the tipless type microcantilever sensor exhibits a high Q-factor value. In a closed system, the average Q-factor is 248.67, whereas in an open system, it reaches 251,812. The analysis of the Q-factor also indicates remarkable stability with minimal damping.This research provides evidence that utilizing a tipless type microcantilever sensor in a particle detection system yields a stable response and a high Q-factor value. This highlights the sensor’s potential for applications in portable particle detection.

articleTitle: Influence of the Quenching Process on the Local Structure and Thermoelectric Properties of Polycrystalline LaCoO3
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We succeeded in synthesizing polycrystalline LaCoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> using the solid-state method which was then carried out various heat treatments with and without a quenching process. The powder X-ray diffraction spectrum shows that the peak formed is LaCoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with a rhombohedral crystal structure with the space group $R-3 C$. The results of the Rietveld refinement exhibit the sample that underwent the quenching process $(Q)$ produced a cell volume that was larger than that without quenching (NQ). For distances and angle bonding on the NQ sample, it is $1.9342(17)$ Å and $163.8(7)^{\circ}$, while for the sample Q, it is $1.93386(0)$ Å and $163.8023(0)^{\circ}$, respectively. The particle sizes of both samples are in the order of $\mu \mathrm{m}$-units. The EDX measurement results show that the ratio between the La and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> elements is slightly non-stoichiometric. The quenching process causes a slight decrease in resistivity which has a direct impact on increasing the $P F$ value. The largest $P F$ of Q and NQ samples is about $0.0398 \mathrm{~mW} / \mathrm{mK}^{2}$ and $0.0317 \mathrm{~mW} / \mathrm{mK}^{2}$, respectively.

articleTitle: Design Microcantilever Array based Carbon Nanotubes for Detection of Heavy Metal Ions in Water
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Water contamination by Heavy Metal Ions (HMIs) is one of several environmental problems that almost all countries are currently dealing with, and a majority of these countries are finding it extremely difficult to resolve. In this work, we design and simulate a microcantilever array based on Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) for the detection of HMIs for mass ranges between 0 to 100 $\mu g$ using COMSOL multiphysics. The sensor is designed and a comparative study is analyzed with different silicon compounds (like silicon and silicon dioxide) with layer coating to target heavy metal ions, the mechanical displacement under the pressure action of the target ions was used to evaluate the structures. Based on the simulation result, the device achieves a linear characteristic response and high sensitivity, the sensitivity for silicon and silicon dioxide is 0.37 and $0.36 \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{Pa}$ respectively.

articleTitle: Search and Rescue (SAR) Flight Simulations Utilizing Low-Budget Autonomous Quadcopter and Image Processing Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In Search and Rescue operations, designated search areas are explored by aircraft and helicopters. Upon target identification, the aerial platform proceeds with the landing and rescue procedure. This research employs a quadcopter to replicate SAR flight scenarios. The quadcopter’s autonomous operation encompasses takeoff and navigation between waypoints as dictated by the Mission Planner software. En route to the second waypoint, a camera-based image processing system scans the ground. Detection of a ground marker activates the Raspberry Pi program, instructing the flight controller to ensure precise landing directly over the recognized marker. In cases where the quadcopter reaches the second waypoint but the system fails to identify a ground marker, the programmed response involves the quadcopter autonomously returning to the initial waypoint, where it executes a self-guided landing at its takeoff location. A captivating aspect of this investigation concerns the efficacy of a cost-effective 5 Megapixel camera, with a $1280\times 720$-pixel frame, in accurately identifying landing markers. The study’s parameters encompass marker diameter, flight altitude, and quadcopter speed. Outcomes demonstrate successful marker detection at flight altitudes up to 3 meters above ground, achieving a top speed of 3 m/s at a 2-meter height. The smallest identifiable marker diameter remains at 40 cm.

articleTitle: Improving Load Power Sharing Accuracy in Standalone Microgrid DC Networks Using Intelligent Adaptive Droop Control Based on Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: DC Microgrid refers to a network that connects distributed DC generators. The control of the DCMG converters is employed to achieve proportional load sharing and optimal DC bus voltage restoration. Conventional droop control is a common technique used in DC Microgrids with multiple converter units. However, the performance of this technique is limited when considering channel resistance differences. In this article, we propose an adaptive droop control that utilizes secondary control to minimize DC bus voltage deviation while improving load power-sharing accuracy. The droop resistance is adjusted using a proportional controller to compensate for load current sharing errors while reducing DC bus voltage deviation through a PI controller. To determine the actual load current conditions, the exchange of output currents between converter units through communication channels is taken into account. The proposed control strategy can maintain a balanced load power distribution among the three sources with a ratio close to 1:1:1. Comparative analysis results between the conventional droop control method and the proposed method are fully simulated in Matlab/Simulink with varying load power values.

articleTitle: A Filtenna Design for Ku-Band Satellite Mobile Terminal
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a filtenna (filtering antenna) design for Ku-Band satellite mobile terminal. The filtenna was designed to decrease the size of the device. Hence, the manufacturing cost can be reduced. The electromagnetic software was used to validate and optimize the design on the RT/duroid 5880 as a substrate. In this structure, the feed line of the antenna becomes the input port of the filter. Furthermore, the multimode resonator (MMR) was integrated into the antenna to eliminate undesired frequencies in certain bandwidths. The connection between the filter ports and the MMR used a coupled method. From the simulation results, the bandpass filter is successfully attached to the antenna. So, it reduced the size and manufacturing cost. The reflection coefficient ($\text{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$) at operating frequency has good agreement with the specification. However, the bandwidth is slightly different. The bandwidth of filtenna is bigger, 40 MHz, than the specification. The proposed design has a dimension of 37.7 mm $\times 21$ mm. For future research, the fabrication process will be done to realize the design.

articleTitle: 38 GHz Wideband and High Gain Stacked Antenna Modelling for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper introduces the design features of a novel stacked antenna that possesses highly compact broadband and omnidirectional radiation properties. The proposed antenna covers a wide frequency range of 34 to 44 GHz, encompassing dual potential bands in the 5G spectrum such as 36, and 38 GHz. The proposed antenna has a simple design process, low complexity, and desirable features such as a wide impedance bandwidth, and omnidirectional radiation. These qualities make it suitable for fulfilling the requirements of 5G applications. The achieved minimum gain is 6 dBi for the entire frequency range of operation.

articleTitle: Automatic Bow Echo Shape Detection Using Combination of Image Processing and Skeletonization in X-Band Radar Image
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Image acquisition from the rain scanner radar Santanu could capture the bow echo shape that manifestation of heavy precipitation and strong wind. An alternative method to automatically detect the bow echo using image radar has been proposed in this study. The method combines image processing and skeletonization. Image processing is used to identify all the objects, restructure the elements, label, and calculate their properties including the estimated length and eccentricity. Skeletonization is used to represent the basic shape of an object, combined with curve angle detection to estimate the bending factor of an object. The proposed method has been tested using 80 radar images from the observation period of 2020 until 2022 in the Bandung area. Statistical analysis is carried out to obtain the threshold of curve angle and eccentricity. From six combinations of this threshold, 41 images (51.25%) of bow echo can be detected automatically. The threshold that affects the detection result is the lower threshold of curve angle and eccentricity. However, this setting gives a more realistic result because lower curve angle and lower eccentricity value will outcome a V-shape object detection which is undesirable.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Polarimetric Ground Based Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging using Portable VNA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the findings of a comprehensive polarimetric Ground-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GBSAR) imaging study conducted using a portable Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) as the primary radar instrument. The study was undertaken to acquire preliminary knowledge in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensor technology at the Indonesian National Research and Innovation Agency for environmental remote sensing monitoring. In this study, we employed four corner reflectors and two tiny Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) as our designated targets. The data-gathering process was conducted in a strip-map stop-and-go mode, utilizing a portable two-port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) and two horn antennas. The study was conducted within a controlled indoor setting to assess the focusing capabilities and obtain polarimetric picture data. The Back-Projection Algorithm (BPA) is subsequently employed to acquire the image outcomes and validate the position of each target. Theoretical analysis was conducted on the geometrical configuration of the test, and initial considerations were made regarding the strategies for focussing. Ultimately, the campaign outcomes were processed and analyzed, yielding results that align closely with the underlying theoretical framework.

articleTitle: Terahertz Propagation Investigation of Terahertz Imaging on A Cancer Object
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Cancer is one of the most challenging diseases in the world. Cancer mortality can be reduced with early detection; hence, when cancer is detected in its early stages, there is a higher chance of recovery. Terahertz technology offers a potential solution for creating a cancer imaging technique, leveraging its benefits. Cancer imaging techniques have been developed to establish terahertz imaging systems. Nevertheless, limited studies still explore the propagation phenomenon of terahertz radiation. This research investigates terahertz propagation for cancer imaging by simulating various system scenarios. The results reveal several phenomena, including wave diffraction and interference, significantly impacting the imaging outcomes. Among the simulated scenarios, the most optimal configuration is achieved with an 11.5 mm source-to-object distance and a 1.5 mm sensor-to-object distance, with a standard deviation 12.327. This research serves as a valuable reference for the development of terahertz imaging systems in the future.

articleTitle: Time Synchronization for OFDM Systems Using the Symmetric Correlator-ELM Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Time synchronization at receivers has a substantial impact on system performance in multicarrier communication systems like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based systems. An extreme learning machine (ELM)-based synchronization technique is suggested to prevent multipath channel disruption and ensure time synchronization. In this study, the coarse feature of the synchronization metric is the symmetric correlator. Then, to lessen the impact of multipath channels, an ELM-based network is used. This technique does not require information from channel statistics, and labeling on the ELM network does not require channel length information. According to experimental findings, our strategy might greatly lower the error probability of time synchronization when compared to earlier approaches.

articleTitle: U-Net Utilization on segmentation of Aerial Captured Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A Convolutional Neural Network based on U-Net architecture was implement for object segmentation on Aerial captured Images. The architecture was modified by adding several dropout layers. The combination of several activation function, optimizer, and loss function was tested on the network, and the best combination giving Sorensen Dice Coefficient score of 0.86656 for the test set.

articleTitle: The Effect of Dineohexyl Phosphinic Acid on the Photovoltaic Performance of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells Based on Organic Dyes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Dineohexyl phosphinic acid (DINHOP) is a dye additive widely used for dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSC) based on ruthenium dyes. Although the effect of DINHOP on the improvement of DSSC based on ruthenium dyes performance has been well demonstrated, the effect of DINHOP on the DSSC based on organic dyes performance is not yet clear. In this work, we used DINHOP as a surface modifier and anchoring group to enhance the performance of DSSC based on organic dyes. We used squaraine dyes SQ2, a purely organic pigment (Solaronix). Dye solutions of different molar ratios SQ2:DINHOP were prepared and used for sensitization of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film. The presence of a DINHOP surface modifier decreases the absorbance peak of SQ2 due to the competition of DINHOP adsorption with the SQ2 dyes. The DSSC fabricated with SQ2:DINHOP 2:1 dye solution enhanced the DSSC performance up to 70% compared to the DSSC free of surface modifier as reference. The obtained efficiency, FF, Jsc, and Voc are 1.62%, 66,8%, 2.06 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 590.9 mV, respectively. DINHOP is a powerful surface modifier due to the prevention against recombination across TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/electrolyte interface only if co-sensitized with dye in a very high concentration of DINHOP. After one month of fabrication, the efficiency of DSSC with DINHOP surface modifier is below the efficiency of reference DSSC. The existence of the DINHOP surface modifier may be responsible for the rapid reduction of short-circuit current density.

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Analysis of Microstrip Antenna Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this paper, a methodology is proposed to design the pattern of a microstrip antenna using the approach of generating synthetic data based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Initially, we provide the model with a dataset developed with various geometries associated with the RO303 substrate. With this, the generator will be able to synthesize new samples that resemble the training set, and it can learn the patterns and relationships between the geometries and their characteristics. One of the main advantages of this approach is the ability to quickly explore a wide range of antenna designs. By using GANs, we can generate multiple antenna geometries in a short period, enabling an efficient search for the best solutions that meet the specific project requirements.

articleTitle: Design and Realization Bandpass Filter 2.4 GHz Using Symmetric Step Impedance Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper shows the design, simulation, and realization of a bandpass filter that uses the stepped impedance resonator method, where both resonators are made to be the same shape and symmetric. This bandpass filter is designed and realized to be able to work in the S-band frequency range, mainly working at frequencies 2.4 GHz. The same form of a bandpass filter system is intended to get a better response, including response bandwidth, insertion loss, and return loss. This bandpass filter is designed using materials from Duroid Roger 4350, which has a dielectric constant ($\varepsilon_{r}$) of 3.66 and has a thickness of 1.527 mm. The design is performed to simulate several filter responses for a return loss of 22.047 dB, insertion loss of −0.77 dB at 2.4 GHz, and a bandwidth of 180 MHz.

articleTitle: Directive Beam Metamaterial Inspired Transparent Folded Dipole Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A directive beam compact transparent antenna patch with a circular ring resonator using metamaterial design is presented. The structure consists of a planar folded dipole antenna and the circular ring resonator on the bottom side of the glass substrate, which has a dielectric constant (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 5.6 and a thickness of 0.7 mm, with Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) materials in the patch as the cell unit, which has a thickness of 185 nm. This presented a design simulation for the antenna at mm-wave communication system 28 GHz, which has a bandwidth from 25.31 GHz to 31.92 GHz. In this paper, several simulation sections are executed, including simulations on the planar folded dipole antenna at the top of the substrate, the circular ring resonator at the bottom of the substrate, and the combined two designs. Each of these is carried out to determine the effect obtained so that it can be analyzed. Metamaterial structure is used in the antenna patch for bandwidth, gain, and resonator size reduction. In this design simulation, the effect of the unit cell on the bottom side of the glass substrate with an ITO resonator will be analyzed. The simulation and design have a response S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> at 28 GHz of -25.84 db.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Rain Scanner Radar Performance for Reflectivity-Rainfall Estimation in A Co-Location Grid Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study examines the performance and calibration of rain scanner radar in observing rainfall spatially. The six rain gauges are used as a reference for validating the radar performance in estimating rainfall. The data period utilized for this investigation is from January to December 2021. The rainfall data from rain gauges is used to produce the relationship equation between reflectivity and rainfall intensity based on dimensionless radar output (DRO) and rainfall depth (d). The calibration parameter ($\beta$) is determined by performing a linear regression between the accumulated DRO and the accumulated rainfall depth. Generally, RSR accumulated reflectivity aligns well with the rain gauge monthly rainfall pattern. RSR is capable of detecting rainfall with varying intensity at distances of up to 28 km. However, the results of the calibration method using a linear approach between rainfall and DRO tend to underestimate the rainfall.

articleTitle: Development of Controllable LED Light Source for Retinomorphic Sensor Measurement Test
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In the digital age, the advancement of autonomous vehicles is currently extremely quick. The invention and development of retinomorphic sensors lend credence to this. This sensor’s ability to function similarly to the human eye makes it handy for detecting the presence of objects in front of the sensor. It is necessary to use a tool known as an LED controller to test this sensor. To evaluate the voltage regulation on the LED controller both mechanically and digitally, this research will explore, design, and construct an LED controller. The LED Controller has voltage adjustment capabilities between 1.2 and 25 volts. However, the highest power the LED can withstand is somewhere between 15 and 16 volts. As a result, 16 Volts should be set as the input limit value in the microcontroller program.

articleTitle: Initial Coverage Analysis of LoRa Communication for Light Buoy Monitoring System in Port Area
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The light buoy is a vital navigational aid for ships during port ingress and egress. Its susceptibility to disturbances, location shifts, and even vandalism underscores the necessity for a comprehensive monitoring system for the light buoy. Moreover, these light buoys are typically positioned at considerable distances up to 10 KM from the seashore. Hence, any devised monitoring system must incorporate a communication framework with extended coverage and energy efficiency. In the context of this research, preliminary tests were conducted to assess the communication range of LoRa within port areas to support the monitoring system for light buoys. A LoRa node was developed, equipped with a GPS sensor to ascertain its positioning. Subsequently, this node was mobilized from the harbor towards the port’s shipping lane to gauge the extent of LoRa communication within that region. The experiments revealed that LoRa communication could span long distances up to the farthest light buoy (9.51 KM) with poor received data rate. Despite the less favorable outcomes observed in the test results, given the potential variability in parameters and conditioning, the experiments underscore that LoRa communication remains the most promising means for transmitting monitoring data from light buoys.

articleTitle: EEG Analysis based on Spectral Edge Frequency during Mental Arithmetic Task
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Brain dynamics variables and features are critical in electroencephalogram (EEG)-based human cognition research. They allow researchers to investigate how functionality changes based on the environment and how a task is carried out. This work gives a unique perspective of EEG analysis based on spectral edge frequency 50% (SEF50) methodologies to examine the differentiation of brain electrical activity during mental arithmetic task based on two circumstances (a) rest and task; and (b) mental arithmetic task success rate. According to our findings, the spectral edge frequency of the signals is increasing in beta and gamma-wave activity during mental arithmetic activities compared to rest state. In terms of performance, trends in the SEF50 curves indicate that average performers and bad performers likely expend more cognitive effort than good performers, particularly in higher-frequency ranges. Notably, the data revealed that frontal and pre-frontal brain regions indicate the brain activity compare to other brain regions. In conclusion, the SEF50 techniques used in this research are insightful and can be regarded as a feature of EEG data.

articleTitle: Motion Capture Systems with IMU Sensors: A Preliminary investigation of Oil Palm harvesting Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Motion capture systems employing Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensors have found increasing utility in agricultural tasks, including oil palm for assessing occupational risks. However, research in this domain remains limited. This study aimed to conduct an initial observational assessment to predict the potential risk of injury based on joint contact force parameters in oil palm harvesting, specifically in the push technique. IMU data along with force data were processed using inverse dynamic technique through the utilization of the Biomechanics of Bodies (BoB) to calculate joint contact forces. The findings revealed that the work experience of the harvester and the cutting technique employed influence the potential injury in oil palm harvesting. These results underscore the necessity for further investigation to identify optimal harvesting techniques in oil palm harvesting that minimize the risk of work-related injuries.

articleTitle: On Modeling a Bottleneck Link using Dummynet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Developing a communication network of any system must continue to improve capability and scalability. However, development without a plan will cost a lot of energy and costs; this requires a testing system implemented as a network testbed. Testbeds are classified into two, namely physical testbed and virtual testbed, where virtual testbed is superior in terms of cost and scalability. To create network links in a virtual testbed, we propose using Dummynet which can emulate real network conditions. Performance comparisons were made between a particular Mikrotik router (as a physical device representation) and Dummynet using virtual machine (VM). Experiment results show that Dummynet is better in terms of bandwidth-limiting accuracy, with 95.56% to 97.16% accuracy, compared to Mikrotik router, with 91.09% to 95.07% accuracy. On the other hand, Mikrotik router has the advantage of a relatively stable packet delay. In contrast, Dummynet has an additional delay with a maximum value of 6.06 ms at 64 Kbps bottleneck bandwidth. Dummynet is still relevant for implementing network links in a virtual testbed, when physical delays are above that measured additional delay.

articleTitle: PI Controller Design for MIMO process on the Autoclave Passivation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Passivation Autoclave is a device used to passivate (make passive) the surface of the nuclear fuel element beam cladding, so that the metal surface will have a low corrosion rate. This autoclave system is a heating furnace with a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) $3 \times 3$ model. System identification is performed experimentally directly on the device to derive a mathematical model in the form of a first-order transfer function. The inverted decoupling technique is used to reduce interactions in the MIMO model, followed by the implementation of PI control within this mathematical model. The control simulation results for the ramp function, with a temperature increase rate of $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ per hour at a temperature setting of $200^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, indicate a steady-state error of $7.8{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and $36.5{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Experiments for PI control testing were conducted directly using the ramp function, with a temperature increase rate of $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ per hour at a temperature setting of $200^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The results of this experiment indicated that the steady-state error for each of the three outputs averaged 1.15%, with the largest error observed in output y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at $195.24^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, or 2.38%. The steady-state error value, which is below 5%, meets the achievement criteria which shows the performance results of the control scheme

articleTitle: Study on Thick Film Humidity Sensor using PVA-Gelatin-SnO2 Sensing Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this research, various compositions of sensing layers have been studied for their use in humidity sensors. Materials used for the sensing layers were Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA), Gelatin, and Tin Oxide (SnO2). The sensor device was designed and fabricated using thick film technology through screen printing techniques on Alumina (Al2O3) substrates, with Silver-Palladium (AgPd) as the electrode material. The number of electrode fingers was varied to obtain optimum sensor resistance values. The PVA sensing layer was combined with gelatin and various compositions of SnO2 to study their effect on the sensor response to humidity. The sensor devices were tested in a custom chamber with varying humidity levels from 50% to 90%. The results showed that the sensor based on the PVAGelatin-SnO2 (PGS) sensing layer had higher resistance values and more sensitive responses than the sensor without gelatin. The hydrophilic nature of gelatin has been found to contribute significantly to the water sensitivity of the matrix. In addition, the difference in the number of fingers of the sensor electrode and the addition of SnO2 also affect the resistance value.

articleTitle: Precise Temperature Control Strategy for Laboratory-Scale Fermentation Process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a precise temperature control strategy for a laboratory-scale fermentor system. The proposed method utilizes actuators employing a hysteresis on/off cooling mechanism and a proportional derivative (PD) control algorithm enhanced with range-time proportional heating control. The objective of the control strategy is to achieve a stable point temperature of 28 to $30 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ within the fermentation chamber, with a maximum steady-state error allowed at $1 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method in accurately regulating the temperature inside the fermentation chamber. The system achieves the desired temperature in 3600 seconds when cooled with a set point of $30 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, but takes 5 times longer with the lowest set point of temperature, with a maximum overshoot of less than $0.3 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ or 1% from the operational set point and a steady-state error of $0.25 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Future research can further enhance the stability of the fermentation process by incorporating optimal tuning methods. The developed precise heating control strategy has practical implications for the laboratory-scale fermentor, contributing to improved process efficiency and product quality. It also provides the foundation for potential applications in larger-scale industrial fermentation.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of NOMA-assisted Overlay Communication in Energy-Limited Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a promising communication technique that has gained attention in recent years, particularly in the context of energy-limited networks. This approach permits several devices to share the same frequency and time resources, enabling improved spectral efficiency, energy efficiency, and communication reliability. The paper evaluates the performance of NOMA-assisted overlay communication in such networks in terms of innumerable pivotal performance metrics. Numerous results demonstrated the considerable effects of distinct system parameters on the performance of this communication.

articleTitle: Image Super Resolution Using ESRGAN: A Preliminary Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The ongoing progression of technology has led to substantial advancements in image and video quality. Elevated image and video quality inherently enhance visual experiences. However, not all visual content maintains a high standard. Diverse factors contribute to the degradation of image and video quality. Nevertheless, super-resolution techniques offer a solution to restore compromised quality in images and videos. Super-resolution involves enhancing low-resolution images into high-resolution versions, often achieved through deep learning-based methodologies. This research focuses on utilizing the Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN) to elevate image quality, providing the potential for generating images of superior quality from low-resolution sources.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Machine Learning-Aided Flow Traffic Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In recent years, machine-learning algorithms have been developed for application-level traffic generators, but have yet to be implemented in flow-level traffic generators. Since flow-level traffic data is a time series traffic data, it could be used for predicting subsequent network traffic. Its prediction ability can be utilized to generate traffic when the database cannot provide the data. This is an improvement from our previous work that uses exact-database methods which only generate traffic data based on the database. A comparison is made between traditional machine-learning methods (Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, and Gaussian Process Regression) and a deep-learning method (Long-Short Term Memory) to determine how well the Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm performs when applied to a flow-level traffic generator. These methods enable traffic generators to continue generating traffic while the database is unavailable. Among all the methods, the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm performs the best because it has the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value which is 0.13. Visually, some traditional machine learning methods still manage to imitate real traffic, despite their high RMSE values.

articleTitle: Axial-Ratio Beamwidth Enhancement of Circular Polarized Microstrip Antenna Using Periodic Conducting Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A circularly polarized microstrip antenna with a series of conducting structures and a ground slot is proposed in this paper. The series of conducting posts enhances the 3dB beamwidth and axial ratio (AR) value, but the AR beamwidth is limited. The introduction of a ground slot enhances the AR beamwidth with minimal alteration to the 3dB beamwidth. The proposed antenna has a uniform 3dB beamwidth at all azimuth axes greater than 130 degrees, and the AR beamwidth is also uniform up to 86 degrees. The introduction of a ground slot in the antenna design resulted in a 60 percent improvement in the axial ratio AR beamwidth.

articleTitle: Cognitive Linear Trajectory on GPR Imaging Using Lightweight Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a mature technology for exploring subsurface objects. However, in the case of very large observation areas such as in building health assessment or subsurface utility inspection, a fast and effective sensing method is needed. This paper reports the preliminary study of adaptive linear trajectory on the GPR imaging aiming to fasten the scanning process without losing the buried object image details. By employing a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to A-scan data, the possibility of object’s existence was estimated to retune the speed of linear scanning of GPR to produce detailed radar images. Based on the evaluation of the synthetic data, the method can detect the object's existence with accuracy more than 80%. Still, to be implemented in the real applications, some improvements and advancements of the technique are required.

articleTitle: Cognitive Load Assessment through Power Spectral Density in EEG
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Cognitive load (CL) is a key concept in evaluating and tracking human performance in cognitive activities. The goal of this study was to assess cognitive strain using EEG signals from an existing mental arithmetic dataset. Our evaluation included examining the PSD values of theta and alpha frequency bands across all channels. We also investigated the theta-to-alpha ratio in three electrode configurations: Fz, Pz, Cz, and a mix of frontal and parietal electrodes for both the left and right brain hemispheres. The assessments were conducted in two conditions: (i) resting vs task; and (ii) based on distinct performance levels. Our main findings revealed that, when compared to the rest state, the PSD values for the theta and alpha frequency bands decreased during the task state, while the theta-to-alpha ratio increased. This means that individuals had increased cognitive load and decreased relaxation.Furthermore, when assessing CL during a single subtraction task, the left brain hemisphere appeared to be more active than the right. The secondary observation found that good performers, as opposed to average and bad performers, had peak PSD values in both theta and alpha frequency bands, as well as the theta-to-alpha ratio. This shows that good performers bear a heavier cognitive load than their peers, which is consistent with the observation that their left hemisphere is more engaged than the others. Finally, the methods used in this study are insightful and can be considered a feature of EEG data.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Backpropagation Neural Network Training Algorithm for EEG-Based Drowsiness Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Drowsiness, a major cause of car accidents, is detectable through EEG signal feature classification. This study emphasizes machine learning for EEG signal analysis, focusing on Power Spectral Density (PSD) in different frequency band combinations. Backpropagation is employed for classification, with a comparison of various training algorithms like Levenberg-Marquardt (LM), Resilient Backpropagation (RP), Scaled conjugate gradient propagation (SCG), and Conjugate Gradient Backpropagation Fletcher-Reeves updates (CGF). The CGF algorithm achieves the highest accuracy for both Oz and Fz EEG channels, with Oz at 75% accuracy (learning rate 0.4, training time 5.56 seconds) and Fz at 71.6% accuracy (learning rate 0.7, training time 4.93 seconds). This research advances the field by comparing training algorithms within Backpropagation, highlighting their influence on system accuracy, and evaluating the performance of Fz and Oz EEG channels, providing insights for drowsiness detection and driver safety research.

articleTitle: Wheel Odometry-Based Localization for Autonomous Wheelchair
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Localization is a fundamental requirement for an autonomous vehicle system. One of the most often used systems for autonomous vehicle localization is the global positioning system (GPS). Nevertheless, the functionality of GPS is strongly dependent on the availability of satellites, making it unreliable in some situations. As a result, autonomous vehicles must possess autonomous self-localization capabilities to ensure their independent operation. Odometry techniques are employed to achieve vehicle localization by predicting the vehicle position and orientation based on sensor measurements of the vehicle motion. One of the approaches employed in odometry is known as wheel odometry. Wheel odometry has a lower degree of reliance on the surrounding environment than visual odometry and laser odometry. This study aims to evaluate the performance of wheel odometry implementation for an autonomous wheelchair in the context of the localization process. The differential drive kinematic model is employed to determine the predicted pose of a wheelchair. This prediction is derived from the measurement of the linear and angular velocity of the wheelchair. Several experiments have been conducted to evaluate the performance of wheel odometry-based localization. Prior to experimenting, calibration procedures have also been performed to ensure accurate measurements of the sensor.

articleTitle: VIIRS Day/Night Band Image Processing System for Boat Detection in Java Sea, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: VIIRS is a sensor onboard NOAA JPSS satellite series. Day/Night Band (DNB) is one of VIIRS outputs that offers overnight monitoring of quantitative low visible and near-infrared light emitted by the earth’s surface. VIIRS DNB composites can generally be used for visual interpretation. In order to get better interpretation and precise result, this paper provides a development of VIIRS DNB image processing system for boat detection in Java Sea, Indonesia. Boat detection is chosen as the preliminary target of this image processing since the light presence in the ocean is brighter than the background. An image processing system was developed to process the raw data of VIIRS DNB in SDR (Sensor Data Record) and EDR (Environmental Data Record) level. Pre-processing and mask-processing are two main processes implemented in this system. Radiance value of VIIRS DNB is applied to mathematical operations as well as wiener and median filters during the preprocessing step. In mask-processing, the system focuses on categorizing and eliminating other lights such as lightning, gas flare, and ionospheric energetic particle using some thresholds based on spike height index (SHI). During the implementation, by taking a sample area in Western Java Sea, an average of 454 boats is detected at night. The image processing time takes less than 4 minutes for one input data. The output data come in CSV format including longitude and latitude of boat, which can be used to monitor marine activities at nighttime and help stakeholders to counter illegal fishing in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control Strategy for Underactuated AUVs to Overcoming Environmental Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) have transformed marine operations, from deep-sea exploration to environmental monitoring. However, the unpredictable underwater currents and environmental uncertainties pose formidable challenges, especially for underactuated AUVs. This paper introduces a groundbreaking hybrid control strategy amalgamating Line-of-Sight (LOS), Linear Discrete Model Predictive Control (LDMPC), and the Pole-Placement Method. This triad approach is designed to leverage the unique strengths of each method, offering superior resilience against environmental vagaries. Through rigorous simulations, mainly mimicking ocean current disturbances, our results demonstrate the strategy’s exceptional robustness. The AUV’s trajectory mirrored the desired path in pristine conditions, emphasizing the control strategy’s effectiveness. Despite disturbances, the strategy proved adept at counteracting external disruptions, ensuring steadfast and secure navigation. This research marks a significant stride towards enhancing AUVs’ operational efficiency and safety in intricate marine settings.

articleTitle: VRRP-Based WAN Redundancy Protocol for Dual Gateway Cable Based Tsunameter (INA-CBT)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In the new development of the Indonesia cable-based tsunameter (INA-CBT), a double landing stations (LS) configuration will be implemented. Along with this new configuration, there is a necessity for a WAN redundancy protocol to fully draw its potential. The common approach is by using the first-hop redundancy protocol (FHRP) family, and in this research, virtual router redundancy protocol (VRRP) is used. In the basic VRRP protocol, the mechanism to do a failover that is triggered by a wide area network (WAN) connectivity failure is not supported. Therefore in this paper, we combine the basic VRRP protocol with a Netwatch feature on RouterOS Mikrotik to answer the new INA-CBT technical challenge for a WAN redundancy protocol. The VRRP configuration is implemented on a virtual test bed that resembles the new development of INACBT network topology. In addition, real link latency and packet loss quality of service (QoS) metrics of INA-CBT Labuanbajo optical and satellite links were simulated in this testbed by using a network software emulator named GNS3. We evaluated the WAN redundancy protocol performance by measuring failover time, failback time, and downtime experience by the landing station. In each measurement, three test parameters were varied to know the impact of each parameter on the performance. We discover from this test that ping and advertisement interval significantly impact performance, but link latency impact is negligible. For all of the test parameter values that were used, The performance complies with the criteria of INA-CBT data transmission requirements that it must be less than 6 minutes, even in our worst configuration parameter. As for the best performance, we got a downtime value of 2.88 s.

articleTitle: Preparation of Symmetric and Asymmetric Porphyrin as a Passivating Agent for Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Porphyrin is a macromolecular heterocyclic compound with broad applications, such as photocatalyst, photodynamic therapy agent, and photosensitizer in solar cells. Synthesis of symmetric porphyrins, such as meso-tetraphenylporphyrin and meso-tetra(4-methoxyphenyl) porphyrin was carried out using a one-pot Microwave-Assisted Organic Synthesis (MAOS) method. Meanwhile, asymmetric porphyrins were synthesized using a common reflux method by applying 5-phenyldipyrromethane as the precursor to control the asymmetric porphyrin products. Separation and purification of synthesized porphyrin were performed using column chromatography. Preliminary analysis of the synthesis results was carried out by thin layer chromatography (TLC), UV-Vis spectroscopy, and fluorescence analysis.
